title: Monthly resource position is followed by distinct earnings and hours movement across work-limiting status
source_unit: Identified 2025 SIPP person, resource band at month t to valid numeric earnings/hours change at month t+1, conditioned on EDISABL

observations.period: 2024 reference year; resource band at month t to month t+1 earnings/hours change; work-limiting status = yes

denominator.unit: valid earnings pairs; hours outcome uses its own 11,548-pair universe

below_1x_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 4.934 pp; approximate 95% CI 57.034–76.373

1_to_2x_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 3.641 pp; approximate 95% CI 64.195–78.468

2_to_4x_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.572 pp; approximate 95% CI 77.012–83.172

4x_or_more_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.026 pp; approximate 95% CI 83.572–87.595

below_1x_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 2.547 pp; approximate 95% CI 11.890–21.874

1_to_2x_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.116 pp; approximate 95% CI 7.849–12.225

2_to_4x_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.832 pp; approximate 95% CI 7.624–10.885

4x_or_more_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.629 pp; approximate 95% CI 6.377–8.842

observations.method: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag from THINCPOV to nonnegative numeric TPEARN and TMWKHRS changes, conditioned on EDISABL=yes; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: Earnings and hours use separate valid pair universes. A changed value does not reveal direction, desired hours, job quality, accommodation, or why the change occurred.
observations.subgroup: Persons reporting a work-limiting condition in month t; resource bands retain separate pair universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: High change shares at higher resource bands can reflect larger measured earnings or hours, job composition, reporting, or more opportunities to change; they are not automatically instability or improvement.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; resource band at month t to month t+1 earnings/hours change; work-limiting status = no

denominator.unit: valid earnings pairs; hours outcome uses its own 154,992-pair universe

below_1x_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.943 pp; approximate 95% CI 57.512–65.127

1_to_2x_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.898 pp; approximate 95% CI 78.055–81.576

2_to_4x_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.550 pp; approximate 95% CI 82.760–84.916

4x_or_more_earnings_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.276 pp; approximate 95% CI 85.671–86.752

below_1x_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.745 pp; approximate 95% CI 10.625–13.548

1_to_2x_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.404 pp; approximate 95% CI 6.395–7.977

2_to_4x_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.198 pp; approximate 95% CI 5.019–5.793

4x_or_more_hours_change.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.138 pp; approximate 95% CI 4.010–4.553

observations.method: Same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag from THINCPOV to nonnegative numeric TPEARN and TMWKHRS changes, conditioned on EDISABL=no; WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: This is a descriptive contrast with distinct earnings and hours universes and potential composition differences. A person replicate weight does not create a household estimate.
observations.subgroup: Persons not reporting a work-limiting condition in month t; resource bands retain separate pair universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower hours-change shares do not prove stable or desirable work, and higher earnings-change shares do not prove improved household room; values may move up or down.

related_sources.claim: The reproduction audit preserves inputs, output hash, valid-pair boundary, fields, and Fay-BRR method.

boundary: This is a same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag, not a causal or household-weighted estimate. EDISABL identifies a reported work-limiting condition, not diagnosis, accommodation, discrimination, or preference. TPEARN and TMWKHRS changes do not establish direction, job quality, desired hours, care response, trust, political action, or institutional remedy.
